text:
I haven't run anything yet. The `gh` login on this Mac mini is a GitHub token already on the machine, so that comes first. Your laptop stays the broker, and the mini joins the pool as a worker.

**Ask before I run these:**

1. **May I sign `gh` out on the Mac mini?** That removes the token from this machine. It doesn't revoke it. If the laptop uses the same token, it keeps working there. Because the token has been on this Mac, you may also want to rotate it at github.com/settings/tokens.
2. **What should the mini's budget be?** Mac minis have no battery, so the boost profile applies whenever it's on. Tell me the everyday and boost memory, and a device name such as `mini`. Without flags, setup uses a quarter of RAM (up to 8 GiB) and half (up to 32 GiB).
3. **Do you want me to run the `sudo` commands, or will you run them in your own terminal?** `sudo -n true` works here, so I can run them.

**Once you say yes:**

```sh
# 1. Check the OS. macOS jobs need macOS 26 or newer for the network filter.
sw_vers -productVersion
tailscale status          # confirm the mini is on the same tailnet as your laptop

# 2. Sign out of GitHub on this Mac (only after your yes).
gh auth logout -h github.com
gh auth status            # should report that you're not logged in

# 3. Install the binary.
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/baney75/tentmaker/main/scripts/install.sh | sudo sh -s -- --no-setup

# 4. Set up as a worker: no forge token, no repos.
sudo /usr/local/bin/tentmaker setup --yes --json --no-gh --device mini --memory 2GiB --boost-memory 8GiB

# 5. Verify on the mini.
/usr/local/bin/tentmaker doctor --json
/usr/local/bin/tentmaker status --json

# 6. Verify from the laptop. The mini should appear with free slots.
tentmaker pool --json
```

The mini picks up jobs only through the laptop, because the laptop holds the token and assigns the work. The mini never talks to GitHub. Setup doesn't need `--repo` or `--token-stdin` for a worker, so no token should reach it. If `setup` asks for a token anyway, stop and tell me; don't paste one.

The `--memory` and `--boost-memory` values in step 4 are my guesses. I'll use whatever you choose in question 2.
